body.statement: Can one construct and evaluate \(\mathfrak J(d,K,\lambda,L)\) with absolute constants so that the full observed-cell polynomial \(Q_L\) approximates \(F_K(q)\) with controlled exact factorial covariance, while its balanced-slice reduction matches normalized dual-prior separation and weighted mixture distance uniformly in \(K\), respects the \(\sqrt K\) Boolean obstruction, and remains stable after localization over arbitrary patient-group masses and propensities satisfying only \(e_{ax}\ge1/(2K)\)? The construction must output finite coefficient tables and a terminating exact certificate routine.
body.justification: This is the genuinely open mathematical content: uniform approximation error alone is insufficient unless the same object controls estimator variance and lower-mixture distinguishability.
body.gap: JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015, WuYang2016, and CaiLow2011 provide scalar templates, while Spalek2008 supplies only the Boolean degree obstruction; none closes their multivariate statistical combination.
body.consumer: A solution closes the presently unmatched region \(2<K<d^2\) and supplies an auditable finite statistic for other sparse maxima over growing coordinate sets.

obligation.what_is_open: A dimension-uniform construction of the finite polynomial tables and normalized dual priors with matching approximation, exact factorial-covariance, target-separation, and weighted mixed-moment bounds throughout \(2<K<d^2\), stable under localization for arbitrary patient-group masses and every propensity vector satisfying only the stated lower overlap.
obligation.obstruction: The proved identities expose but do not control the weighted derivative and moment tails. Uniform approximation alone is insufficient, and the cited OR theorem rules out any fixed-relative-error full-Boolean-cube certificate of degree below \(\sqrt K\). No frozen assumption or established node supplies coefficient envelopes, matching legal priors, product-mixture closeness, or mass-localization control with constants independent of \(K\).
obligation.attempted: The balanced Poisson generating functions were expanded exactly on both primal and dual sides; the full observed-cell falling-factorial covariance was evaluated; the ratio-max extension was checked on the whole orthant; and the Boolean reduction was wired to the sharp published approximate-degree obstruction. These steps leave the simultaneous coefficient/variance and normalized-prior tail construction unresolved.
obligation.partial_result: The exact primal identities are now proved: the balanced lift has bias \(\mathcal E_K(P_L)\) and derivative-weighted variance \(\mathcal W_{K,\lambda}(P_L)\), while the observed-cell lift has the displayed finite covariance matrix for arbitrary local masses and logging.  The exact dual kernel is \(\mathfrak D_{K,\lambda}\), and uniform error below \(1/56\) on the Boolean slice forces degree at least \(\sqrt K\).  What remains unproved is an explicit family of finite coefficient tables and normalized priors whose approximation error, exact factorial covariance, target separation, and weighted moment tail have matching absolute-constant orders uniformly in \(K\), followed by localization over arbitrary \(p_x\) and legal \(e_{ax}\).
